title: Fix the motor's power factor
story: A workshop motor behaves like 16 ohm in series with 38.2 mH on 50 Hz mains: power factor 0.8. A 0.1 ohm sense resistor in the return wire turns the line current into a small voltage at node 'ret'. Put a capacitor across the motor so that, at 50 Hz, the line current drops (ret below -47.7 dB of the source) and comes back in step with the voltage (within 10 degrees). The motor itself must keep working exactly as before.

goals.label: line current reduced (sense voltage below -47.7 dB at 50 Hz)
line current within 10 degrees of the voltage (power factor above 0.98)

hints: On 230 V RMS this motor draws 11.5 A and needs Q = I^2 X = 11.5 x 11.5 x 12 = 1587 var of reactive power.
A capacitor supplies V^2 omega C of reactive power. C = Q / (omega V^2) = 1587 / (314.16 x 230^2), about 95 uF.
Without a capacitor the sense voltage is about -46.1 dB and 37 degrees late. Too big a capacitor makes the current lead and grow again.
